[short] skip 'runs build'

# Set BOLERO_CACHE to a clean directory to ensure that 'bolero build' has work to report.
[!GOOS:windows] env BOLERO_CACHE=$WORK/gocache
[GOOS:windows] env BOLERO_CACHE=$WORK\gocache

# 'bolero build' should use BOLERO_TMPDIR if set.
[!GOOS:windows] env BOLERO_TMPDIR=$WORK/my-favorite-tmpdir
[GOOS:windows] env BOLERO_TMPDIR=$WORK\my-favorite-tmpdir
mkdir $BOLERO_TMPDIR
bolero build -x hello.go
stderr ^WORK=.*my-favorite-tmpdir

# Make BOLERO_TMPDIR a regular file. This prevents the creation of work directories,
# so we can check that certain commands don't create them.
# This simulates running on a full disk or a read-only volume.
rm $BOLERO_TMPDIR
cp hello.go $BOLERO_TMPDIR # any file will do

# 'bolero build' should fail if BOLERO_TMPDIR is read-only.
! bolero build -x .
stderr '^bolero: creating work dir: \w+ '$BOLERO_TMPDIR

# 'bolero list' should only fail if it needs to build something.
bolero list -x .
! stderr 'creating work dir'
stdout m
bolero list -m all
stdout m
! bolero list -x -export .
stderr '^bolero: creating work dir: \w+ '$BOLERO_TMPDIR

# 'bolero clean -cache' and 'bolero clean -modcache' should not fail.
bolero clean -x -cache
! stderr 'creating work dir'
bolero clean -x -modcache
! stderr 'creating work dir'

# 'bolero env' should not fail for specific variables.
# Without arguments, it needs to initialize a builder to load cgo flags, and
# that uses a temporary directory.
! bolero env
stderr '^bolero: creating work dir: \w+ '$BOLERO_TMPDIR
bolero env BOLERO_ROOT

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.15
-- hello.go --
package main
func main() { println("hello") }
